candidates.name: OpenSky Network COVID-19 flight dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: Daily global flight-level records (callsign, ICAO24, origin/destination airport where inferable, first/last-seen times, altitude profile) crowdsourced from 2,500+ ADS-B ground receivers, published by the OpenSky Network / Eurocontrol PRU academic team, coverage from 1 Jan 2019 to present, updated continuously; documented in Strohmeier et al. 2021, Earth System Science Data, DOI 10.5194/essd-13-357-2021. Not a GitHub-committed dataset -- served via an S3-style bucket browser at opensky-network.org, free for research use with attribution. GitHub repos that consume it (e.g. siddharth271101/Covid-19-and-Aviation-Industry, a Spark/EMR pipeline joining it to JHU CSSE COVID case counts, MIT licence, 29 commits) show the pull method.
candidates.why_useful: This is essentially a global daily flight-volume series since 2019 -- a genuine travel-demand proxy usable for gap #10 (airline/rail/road capacity and traffic) and cross-checkable against nights/ADR seasonality and COVID-era base effects; far larger and more current than TSA throughput (already tried and found weak since 2024) because it is global, not US-security-line-only.
candidates.size_hint: multi-TB raw, but aggregatable to daily flight counts per country/airport; ~7 years of daily data
candidates.license: free for research/education with attribution; not a standard OSS licence

candidates.name: skynet (ropensci)
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (rOpenSci-reviewed, 230 commits) providing standardized import/processing functions for US BTS T-100 (monthly domestic+international seats/capacity/enplanements by carrier and route since the 1990s) and DB1B (quarterly origin-destination ticket-price survey since 1993), plus tools to build airline route networks from them. Does not ship the raw BTS files -- users point it at their own downloads -- but removes the biggest friction in using T-100/DB1B (gap #10's named source).
candidates.why_useful: T-100 is the closest thing to genuine 'airline seat capacity by route' public data (monthly, by carrier, domestic+international, free from BTS); this package is a ready-made, tested pipeline for turning it into route-network capacity series that could proxy inbound/outbound travel capacity to Airbnb-relevant markets (esp. US gateway cities, and international routes feeding APAC/LatAm markets).
candidates.size_hint: package code only; BTS source files are monthly CSVs, tens of MB per year
candidates.time_coverage: T-100 from ~1990, DB1B from 1993, both to present (quarterly lag)

candidates.name: dataset-flights-brazil
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed dataset from Brazil's ANAC (national civil aviation agency): anac.csv.lrz (compressed flight records, all registered flights in Brazil), airports.csv (ICAO codes, names, coordinates for every airport appearing in the ANAC records), and air_traffic.graphml (an airport-connection graph weighted by flight counts). 39 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Direct, free, committed domestic flight-volume data for Brazil -- fills part of gap #7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU, specifically Brazil, alongside the Embratur/IBGE sources already flagged) and could proxy inbound tourism/business-travel intensity to Brazilian Airbnb markets.
candidates.size_hint: compressed CSV (lrzip) of unspecified but apparently substantial row count + airport list + graph file
candidates.time_coverage: not stated in README; spans ANAC's public flight-record history
candidates.last_activity: 39 commits, exact last-commit date not surfaced

candidates.name: openflights
candidates.what_it_holds: The classic OpenFlights database: airports.dat (~7,000+ airports worldwide, IATA/ICAO/coords), airlines.dat (~6,000 airlines), routes.dat (~67,000 route pairs, i.e. which airline flies which city pair -- no seat/frequency counts, just route existence). Static snapshot, last meaningfully updated circa 2014, but still the standard free global route-network reference (confirmed via the flightdelay-dbt-warehouse repo, which cites OpenFlights airline reference at 6,162 rows).
candidates.why_useful: Gives a free global city-pair route-network topology that can be combined with T-100/other capacity sources or used as a static baseline for which international gateways connect to which Airbnb-heavy markets; AGPL-3.0 licensed code repo, data itself widely mirrored.
candidates.size_hint: 3 .dat files, tens of thousands of rows combined
candidates.time_coverage: static snapshot, last substantive update ~2014 (stale for current capacity, still useful as network topology)
candidates.license: AGPL-3.0 for code; data conventionally treated as open/attributable
candidates.last_activity: low -- largely dormant, occasional maintenance commits

candidates.name: ourairports-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Daily-updated mirror of OurAirports.com: airports.csv, airport-frequencies.csv, runways.csv, navaids.csv, countries.csv, regions.csv -- global airport reference (86,013 airport rows per a citing repo). 1,757 commits, updated daily via automated pull.
candidates.why_useful: A live, daily-refreshed, public-domain airport reference table (more complete/current than OpenFlights' static airports.dat) useful as a join key for any flight-schedule or ADS-B work keyed to IATA/ICAO codes across Airbnb-relevant gateway cities.
candidates.size_hint: 6 CSVs, ~86k airport rows plus runway/navaid detail
candidates.last_activity: actively maintained, daily automated updates, 1,757 commits

candidates.name: airportsdata
candidates.what_it_holds: 28,298 airport/landing-strip/seaplane-base entries with ICAO/IATA codes, coordinates, timezone, elevation; fork of mwgg/Airports, cross-validated against AIPs/ARINC/IATA/ch-aviation. Distributed as CSV plus a PyPI package.
candidates.why_useful: Another free, actively maintained (199 commits) global airport reference with timezone data -- marginal incremental value over OurAirports/OpenFlights but easy to use as a Python package for any flight-data join work.

candidates.name: traffic
candidates.what_it_holds: Mature Python library (1,605 commits, 512 stars, published in JOSS) for pulling and analysing ADS-B/air-traffic trajectory data directly from the OpenSky Network historical database (via Impala/Trino) and Eurocontrol DDR files, with built-in airspace and airport datasets, trajectory cleaning, and visualization (Cartopy, ipyleaflet, altair, CesiumJS). No large committed dataset, but a well-documented, actively used client that dramatically eases historical OpenSky state-vector pulls.
candidates.why_useful: If the team wants to nowcast global or route-level flight volumes from OpenSky's historical Impala database (deeper history and finer grain than the pre-built COVID-19 CSV dumps), this is the standard tool academics use to do it -- lowers the acquisition cost for gap #10.
candidates.size_hint: library only; pulls are as large as the user's OpenSky query
candidates.time_coverage: OpenSky historical DB back to ~2015 (via Impala access, requires a free research account)

candidates.name: vrs-standing-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Route/airline/airport 'standing data' from the Virtual Radar Server project -- per-callsign route lookups (JSON, e.g. routes/IT/ITY110.json) plus consolidated CSV files for routes and airports, served via GitHub Pages and refreshed hourly (CC0-1.0, 25 commits).
candidates.why_useful: A free, hourly-refreshed callsign-to-route lookup table; useful as a join layer for any ADS-B-derived flight counting work but does not itself carry capacity or volume figures.
candidates.size_hint: small; per-callsign JSON + CSV route/airport tables

candidates.name: FiledRoutesDB
candidates.what_it_holds: Planned dataset of filed flight-plan route pairs (callsign to origin/destination, US air traffic system only) intended to be rebuilt weekly from FAA data, excluding LADD-listed aircraft. As of this check the repo explicitly states 'Nothing is published yet. This repository holds no data' pending FAA clarification on redistribution terms. MIT licensed, 2 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Not usable today -- flagged only because if/when published it would be a free weekly US route-pair dataset; worth a re-check in a future sweep, not actionable now.

candidates.name: Covid-19-and-Aviation-Industry
candidates.what_it_holds: Spark/Airflow/AWS EMR pipeline (MIT, 29 commits) that pulls the OpenSky Network's post-2019-01-01 global flight dataset (2,500+ ADS-B receivers), joins it to JHU CSSE COVID-19 case time series, airport-code and country/continent mapping tables, and Indian state ISO codes, loading incrementally to S3.
candidates.why_useful: A concrete, working example of how to acquire and process the OpenSky COVID-19 global flight dataset at scale (see the top OpenSky COVID-19 entry above) -- useful as a reference implementation rather than a data source in itself.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: companion method for the OpenSky COVID-19 dataset entry above
candidates.geography: global, with an India-specific join table

candidates.name: awesome-flight-data
candidates.what_it_holds: A curated 'awesome list' cataloguing flight-data APIs and providers across categories: seat maps/booking (Duffel, Sabre), schedules/seats/capacity (OAG Flight Info API, Cirium Developer Studio), ADS-B/tracking (Flightradar24 API, OpenSky Network API, FlightAware AeroAPI), and historical schedules (Aviation Edge, aviationstack, AeroDataBox, FlightLabs, AirLabs). No data itself, just a map of where to look, including the one named source in our theme (aviationstack) and the closest thing to a paid seat-capacity API (OAG).
candidates.why_useful: Confirms that true public/free airline seat-capacity-by-route data does not exist on GitHub as a committed dataset -- the closest real feeds (OAG, Cirium) are paid APIs, which narrows this theme's actionable candidates to BTS T-100 (via skynet) and OpenSky-derived flight counts as the realistic free substitutes.

candidates.name: opensky-api
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Python/Java client bindings for the OpenSky Network live REST API (state vectors -- current aircraft positions), GPL-3.0, 175 commits. No committed dataset; as of 18 Mar 2026 requires OAuth2 client-credentials auth (basic auth removed).
candidates.why_useful: The standard client for live OpenSky queries; only useful in combination with the historical Impala/Trino access (see xoolive/traffic) or the pre-built COVID-19 CSV dumps for anything backward-looking, since the live API alone gives only current snapshots.

candidates.name: flightdelay-dbt-warehouse
candidates.what_it_holds: A dbt/DuckDB dimensional warehouse built on the classic nycflights13 dataset (336,776 NYC-area departures in calendar 2013 from EWR/JFK/LGA) plus OurAirports (86,013 rows) and OpenFlights (6,162 airline rows) as dimension sources.
candidates.why_useful: Low incremental value -- nycflights13 is a single US market, single year (2013), already-stale teaching dataset; flagged only because it packages OurAirports+OpenFlights joins cleanly, which the other two entries above already cover better.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: OurAirports and OpenFlights entries above; nycflights13 itself is too old/narrow to be useful

notes: WebSearch was unavailable for this entire scout run -- the tool reported the session's 200-call web-search budget already exhausted before my first query (likely shared across the many parallel scout subagents in this sweep), so all three seed queries (opensky, ADS-B Exchange, flight-schedules-dataset) failed outright. I fell back to: (1) direct WebFetch verification of repos recalled from training knowledge, (2) GitHub's github.com/topics/<tag> pages fetched via WebFetch (these worked reliably and are the bulk of how I found new repos), (3) attempts at DuckDuckGo html/lite (blocked by an anti-bot CAPTCHA every time) and Bing site: search (loaded but the site: operator seemed to be ignored/misfiring, returning irrelevant results like openskycc.com or speedtest.net), and (4) github.com/search?q=... which hit a 429 rate limit after the first two tries and had to be abandoned. Net effect: coverage here leans on topic-page browsing (opensky-network, ads-b, flight-data, flightradar24, t100, aviationstack, airline-industry, air-traffic, airfare, opensky) rather than free-text search, so it is broad on 'what exists under these tags today' but may miss repos that don't carry any of those exact GitHub topic tags, README-only Zenodo/Kaggle pointers, or blog posts. Recommend a future scout with a live WebSearch budget re-run this theme with queries like 'aviationstack kaggle', 'ADS-B exchange historical dump zenodo', 'BTS T-100 replication package github', and 'airline capacity OAG academic dataset' to check for misses. Clear finding either way: true free/open airline SEAT-CAPACITY-by-route data does not appear to exist as a GitHub-committed dataset -- the two real substitutes are BTS T-100 (via ropensci/skynet, US-only, monthly, free from source) and OpenSky-derived flight-count series (global, daily, since 2019, but positions/movements not seats). ADS-B Exchange and FlightRadar24 GitHub presence is almost entirely live-tracking client/hardware projects (Docker feeders, Home Assistant cards, hobbyist radar displays) with essentially no committed historical datasets suitable for backtesting.
